scientific_question: Can occurrence-conditioned finite-world reconstruction correctly retain, eliminate, falsify, or leave unresolved candidate distribution-forming processes when the true virtual process is known?

scope.target: method falsification under known-truth virtual biogeography

reference_implementation.reason: reuse exact EOG finite-world operators and fingerprints; keep one auditable implementation before performance optimization

cpp_port_trigger.trigger: reference benchmark target workload exceeds 60 seconds wall-clock on CI or 1 GiB peak memory
cpp_port_trigger.equivalence_requirement: C++ backend must reproduce all frozen Python fixture classifications and compatible-world sets before use

virtual_system.landscape: finite 2-D grid with explicit coordinates and deterministic environmental fields
virtual_system.niche: declared virtual niche determining viable states
virtual_system.truth_generation: simulate reachable occupied states from one declared true process
virtual_system.observation_generation: sample positive occurrences from true reachable states; primary tests use no false positives
virtual_system.candidate_worlds: finite predeclared alternatives generated from the same process grammar

primary_hypotheses.claim: When the exact true process is included in the candidate universe and observations contain only true positive occurrences, EOG never eliminates the true world at any sequential observation prefix.
primary_hypotheses.decision_rule: SUPPORTED only if 100% of eligible exact benchmark cases retain the true world at every prefix; one counterexample REFUTES the claim for the declared benchmark universe.

primary_hypotheses.claim: When every false candidate has at least one predeclared positive witness occurrence reachable under truth but unsupported by that false candidate, the complete witness set eliminates every false candidate while retaining truth.
primary_hypotheses.decision_rule: SUPPORTED only if 100% of eligible exact benchmark cases end with exactly the true world; one counterexample REFUTES the claim.

primary_hypotheses.claim: When truth is omitted and the predeclared witness set contains at least one true occurrence unsupported by each candidate world, EOG falsifies the entire declared candidate universe.
primary_hypotheses.decision_rule: SUPPORTED only if 100% of eligible exact benchmark cases end with zero compatible worlds; one counterexample REFUTES the claim.

primary_hypotheses.claim: When two or more candidate worlds are observationally equivalent over every available positive occurrence, EOG does not identify a unique world.
primary_hypotheses.decision_rule: SUPPORTED only if 100% of equivalent cases remain non-identifiable; any unique-world declaration REFUTES the claim.

secondary_boundary_hypothesis.claim: False-positive occurrence contamination can invalidate naive positive-only finite-world falsification when observation error is not represented in the declared worlds.
secondary_boundary_hypothesis.purpose: boundary diagnosis, not a requirement for H1-H4
outputs: true-world false-elimination rate by contamination level

prohibited_after_results: add only favorable scenarios to restore support
reinterpret zero compatible worlds as unrestricted biological impossibility
claim a surviving world is the unique historical truth outside the declared finite universe
